title: Endobronchial Valves for Persistent Air Leak and Bronchopleural Fistula in Children: A Systematic Review of Indications, Procedural Approaches, and Outcomes.
authors: Mahindrakar N, Bhandari P, Yedatore R, Vorakunthada Y, Lilitwat W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Persistent air leak (PAL) and bronchopleural fistula (BPF) are uncommon but important complications in children, particularly with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative injury, malignancy, or extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO). When conservative therapy fails or surgery is high-risk, endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement has emerged as a minimally invasive bronchoscopic option. This systematic review summarizes the published pediatric experience, focusing on indications, procedural approach, and outcomes. METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to June 2026, with Google Scholar and reference lists screened; no language limits applied. Eligible studies reported pediatric or late-adolescent patients who underwent bronchoscopic valve placement for PAL, BPF, or pneumothorax with ongoing air leak. Case reports, case series, and observational studies with extractable pediatric data were included. Two reviewers independently screened, assessed eligibility, and abstracted data; findings were synthesized narratively. RESULTS: Thirteen reports were included. Valve placement achieved rapid or eventual air-leak improvement in selected children, including those with necrotizing pneumonia, postoperative air leak, chronic ventilator dependence, malignancy, and ECMO support. Reported complications included valve migration or loosening, granulation tissue, minor hemoptysis, atelectasis, contralateral pneumothorax, and recurrent air leak, although many children underwent valve removal without complication. CONCLUSION: Endobronchial or intrabronchial valve placement may be a useful rescue or bridge therapy for carefully selected children with refractory PAL or BPF. Evidence remains low certainty owing to small samples, retrospective design, inconsistent outcome definitions, and possible publication bias. Prospective multicenter registries with standardized reporting are needed to define optimal selection, timing, and safety.

title: Polycystic ovary syndrome research in sub-Saharan Africa: a systematic review on current status and future directions.
authors: Hatoum S, Amiri M, Makwe CC, Olamijulo JA, Azziz R
journal: Gynecological endocrinology : the official journal of the International Society of Gynecological Endocrinology
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) is one of the most prevalent disorders affecting women. The status of PCOS research in sub-Saharan Africa is unknown, where non-communicable diseases are prevalent but often underrecognized. To assess current knowledge about PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa and identify gaps in the literature. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted across PubMed, Embase, Cochrane, and African Journals Online through 9 August 2026 to identify original studies on PCOS in sub-Saharan Africa. Original research studies involving sub-Saharan African populations, without age-related constraints, were eligible. We excluded non-original studies and studies that did not focus on PCOS. Three independent reviewers (S.H., M.A., and C.C.M.) performed the searches. RESULTS: Of 1973 retrieved records, 40 studies met the inclusion criteria, predominantly from Nigeria, with additional contributions from South Africa, Cameroon, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Tanzania, Benin, Kenya, and Ethiopia. Most studies were observational and primarily focused on PCOS in the context of infertility. No population-based prevalence studies were identified; however, 13 studies reported PCOS prevalence, mostly in clinically selected populations. CONCLUSIONS: PCOS remains understudied in sub-Saharan Africa, with substantial gaps in population-based epidemiology, diagnostic practices, phenotype distribution, management, and metabolic outcomes. Addressing these gaps through larger, well-designed studies is critical to accurately assess the disease burden, inform clinical guidelines, and optimize management strategies. Additionally, overcoming barriers such as cultural attitudes, cost, and limited accessibility to diagnostic tools and treatment options remains essential to improving PCOS care and research across the region.PROSPERO registration ID CRD420250649730 - 13 March 2025.

title: Predicting IGD treatment outcomes across interventions using a whole-brain functional connectome biomarker.
authors: Wei M, Luo X, Fu J, Li S, Ni H, Liu J, Dong GH
abstract: BACKGROUND: Although treatment approaches have been explored in internet gaming disorder (IGD), however, little is known about the specific neural activity that is associated with treatment outcomes. This study aims to establish a treatment-sensitive network that reliably predicts treatment outcomes across different interventions for IGD. METHODS: Resting-state fMRI data were collected from 90 individuals with IGD who received one of three different intervention protocols (mindfulness meditation, approach bias modification, or retrieval-aversive conditioning training). Connectome-based predictive modelling (CPM) was used to build a treatment-sensitive network to predict individual symptom reduction, then validated them on the external dataset. RESULTS: The negative (r = 0.401, p <.001) and combined network (r = 0.480, p <.001) can significantly predict a reduction of addiction severity (baseline minus post-test). Specifically, the negative network was primarily centred on the motor, subcortical, and salience networks. The positive network primarily involved cerebellar-related connections. Incorporating these into a combined model significantly improved predictive accuracy, suggesting that cerebellar-related connectivity may contribute to the prediction of intervention-related clinical improvement. Finally, the treatment-sensitive network was validated in a separate data. CONCLUSIONS: This study established a treatment-sensitive network based on the whole-brain connectome. These findings provide valuable empirical evidence for identifying biomarkers for IGD treatment and advance personalised therapeutic strategies. CLINICAL TRIALS REGISTRATION: The trial protocol was pre-registered with the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (www.chictr.org.cn; ChiCTR2300077831(MM), ChiCTR2300075869(ApBm), ChiCTR2500095444(R-AC), ChiCTR2400090834(SAE)).

title: Primary care effectiveness, multimorbidity, and hospital use in public and private health-care systems in Brazil: a cross-sectional analysis of data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian longitudinal study of aging.
authors: Oliveira GM, Nunes BP, Lam K, Lima-Costa MF, Torres JL, Macinko J, Moreira BS, Avelino-Silva TJ
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether patient-reported experiences in primary care modify the association between multimorbidity and emergency department (ED) visits and hospitalizations remains unclear. We examined these associations across public and private health system sectors among Brazilians aged ≥50 years. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used nationally representative data from the 2019-2021 Brazilian Longitudinal Study of Aging. Multimorbidity was defined as the presence of ≥2 of 13 chronic conditions. A 12-item patient-reported primary care effectiveness index captured access, continuity, communication, and coordination with participants' usual source of healthcare. Primary outcomes were ED visits and hospitalizations in the past 12 months. Poisson regression models estimated associations with the outcomes, and assessed interactions among multimorbidity, primary care effectiveness, and health system sectors. FINDINGS: Among 9058 participants (mean age = 66.3 ± 9.9 years; females = 55.3%; White race/ethnicity = 46.4%), 38.0% had multimorbidity. Overall, 12.5% reported an ED visit and 6.0% ≥ 1 hospitalization in the past 12 months. Multimorbidity was associated with approximately twice the prevalence of ED visits and three times the prevalence of hospitalizations. Primary care effectiveness modified these associations across health system sectors (three-way interaction p = 0.04 for ED visits and p < 0.001 for hospitalization). In the public system, higher primary care effectiveness attenuated the association between multimorbidity and hospitalization (interaction prevalence ratio [PR] = 0.74, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.63-0.87). In contrast, in the private system, higher primary care effectiveness strengthened the associations of multimorbidity with ED visits (interaction PR = 1.40, 95% CI = 1.18-1.66) and hospitalization (interaction PR = 1.75, 95% CI = 1.22-2.50). INTERPRETATION: Associations between multimorbidity and healthcare use varied according to patient-reported primary care experiences and health system sector. FUNDING: The Brazilian National Council for Scientific and Technological Development, the Alzheimer's Association, and the National Institute on Aging.

title: Associations of 24-hour movement behavior composition with depressive symptoms and problematic internet use in Chinese adolescents: A cohort study.
authors: Fang B, Sun Y, Bai Y, Liu WJ, Lin R, Xia W
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Although 24-hour movement behaviors (24-HMB), including sleep, moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA), and screen time, are associated with adolescent mental health, their compositional nature remains insufficiently examined. We investigated the associations of 24-HMB composition with depressive symptoms, problematic internet use (PIU), and their co-occurrence at one-year follow-up. METHODS: In this prospective cohort study, 12,316 adolescents from the Guangzhou Childhood Adolescent Cohort (2019-2025) were included. Baseline sleep duration, screen time, depressive symptoms, and PIU were assessed using questionnaires, and MVPA was estimated from the number of days per week with at least 60 min of activity. After 1 year of follow-up, outcome-specific analytic samples included 9887 adolescents for depressive symptoms, 11,622 for PIU, and 12,316 for co-occurrence, with 2169, 1149, and 845 events, respectively. Nonlinear associations were examined using restricted cubic splines, and stratified compositional logistic regression models and exploratory isotemporal substitution analyses were then conducted using outcome-specific sleep-duration thresholds identified from the fitted spline curves. RESULTS: Sleep showed nonlinear associations, with the predicted odds reaching its nadir at 8.50 h/day for depressive symptoms, 8.81 h/day for PIU, and 8.68 h/day for co-occurrence. The associations of 24-HMB composition differed across sleep-duration strata for depressive symptoms (P for interaction = 0.014), PIU (P for interaction < 0.001), and co-occurrence (P for interaction = 0.004). Among adolescents sleeping below the outcome-specific thresholds, relatively longer sleep was associated with lower odds of depressive symptoms (OR = 0.53, 95% CI: 0.37-0.76), PIU (OR = 0.33, 95% CI: 0.22-0.50), and co-occurrence (OR = 0.50, 95% CI: 0.32-0.79), particularly when replacing screen time. In the lower-sleep strata, relatively longer screen time was associated with higher odds of these outcomes, whereas theoretical reallocations from screen time to the estimated MVPA component were associated with lower odds in exploratory substitution analyses. CONCLUSIONS: Our findings highlight the importance of considering 24-HMB as an integrated composition. The associations of 24-HMB reallocations with mental health outcomes differed across sleep-duration strata. Reducing screen time, with reallocation to sleep or MVPA according to sleep-duration strata, may offer tailored strategies to improve adolescent mental health.

title: Microenvironmental barriers to healing in osteoradionecrosis and opportunities for regenerative intervention.
authors: La Croix AE, Torres Gouveia ME, Bertone PM, Nemanic NM, Bahney CS, Hixon KR
abstract: Osteoradionecrosis (ORN) is a debilitating sequela of radiotherapy (RT) for head and neck cancer (HNC), characterized by persistent bone exposure or radiographic non-viability and profound tissue repair failure. Despite advances in radiation delivery and clinical management, ORN remains challenging to treat, with therapeutic strategies largely focused on symptom control, infection mitigation, or surgical reconstruction rather than restoration of regenerative capacity. Emerging evidence suggests that radiation-induced cellular senescence represents a central and underrecognized driver of ORN pathophysiology. Ionizing radiation disrupts the bone microenvironment through sustained vascular injury, impaired osteogenic-angiogenic coupling, chronic inflammation, and the accumulation of senescent bone-resident and stromal cells that secrete a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Together, these changes create a hostile niche that suppresses bone remodeling and wound healing long after radiation exposure. This review synthesizes current understanding of radiation-induced injury to the bone microenvironment, critically evaluates existing classification systems and treatment strategies for ORN, and examines emerging regenerative approaches. We further propose senotherapeutic strategies targeting radiation-induced cellular senescence as a complementary and potentially transformative avenue to restore tissue repair capacity. By integrating regenerative biomaterials with targeted modulation of senescence, future therapies may move beyond palliation toward true biological resolution of ORN. Biomaterial delivery systems (e.g., injectable hydrogels, mineral composite scaffolds, and cryogel platforms) are emerging as promising vehicles for spatiotemporally controlled senotherapeutic delivery within the irradiated bone niche.

title: Therapeutic Balloon-Assisted Enteroscopy: Recent Advances in the Management of Small Bowel Diseases.
authors: Nagayama M, Kinoshita T, Kawaguchi H, Fujinuma T, Fujikura S, Hayashi H, Tamaru T, Sakamoto H
abstract: Balloon-assisted enteroscopy (BAE) has substantially advanced small bowel disease management. This review summarizes recent therapeutic BAE advances, focusing on three major indications: small bowel vascular lesions, hereditary polyposis syndromes, and Crohn's disease (CD). For suspected small bowel bleeding from vascular lesions, morphological classification guides lesion-specific hemostasis-primarily using argon plasma coagulation and clipping-while gel immersion endoscopy helps secure the visual field. In hereditary polyposis syndromes (e.g., Peutz-Jeghers syndrome and familial adenomatous polyposis), endoscopic ischemic and cold snare polypectomy prevent intussusception and reduce cancer risk, decreasing surgical needs. Additionally, endoscopic balloon dilation is an established bowel-preserving treatment for fibrotic CD strictures, reducing surgical resection and short bowel syndrome risk. Driven by evolving imaging and devices, BAE remains central to small bowel management, improving patient outcomes and quality of life.

title: Recent advances in functionalized electrospun nanofibers for biomedical and therapeutic applications: A comprehensive review.
authors: Deshmukh K, Pandey M, Moulahoum H, Ghorbanizamani F, Kovářík T, Przekora-Kuśmierz A, Jena H, Vora M
abstract: Electrospun nanofibers (ESNFs) have become a major focus of modern research given their adaptable architecture, extensive interface, and distinctive physicochemical characteristics, making them appropriate for varied applications such as catalysis and environmental cleanup, drug delivery (DD), tissue engineering (TE), sensing, actuation, and various energy-related technologies. As a result, electrospinning (ES) has emerged as a versatile manufacturing technique, driving intensive efforts to engineer nanofibrous structures specifically for biomedical purposes. Functionalization of ESNFs can be achieved by embedding functional agents or altering surface chemistry to introduce specific functionalities. This review discusses the fabrication methods, optimization techniques, and broad biomedical applications of modified ESNFs, emphasizing their key properties, including biocompatibility, degradability, and safety profile. The article outlines various strategies for creating and modifying ESNFs, followed by a comprehensive analysis of their applications in tissue regeneration, DD, wound repair, antimicrobial therapy, cancer diagnostics and treatment, and biosensing. By critically evaluating recent advances, highlighting future directions, and addressing ongoing challenges about ES, this review underscores the transformative potential of functionalized ESNFs as efficient and adaptable biomaterials for biomedical technologies.

title: Injectable bioactive glass hydrogels orchestrate metalloimmunotherapy by depleting pathogenic B cells and rescuing bone in rheumatoid arthritis.
authors: Yan Z, Chen Y, Zeng F, Chen Q, Cai H, Qin R, Xu J, Gu B
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is characterized by persistent synovial inflammation and progressive bone destruction. Transcriptomic profiling identified hyperactivated B cells as key contributors to osteoimmune dysregulation, supporting localized B cell intervention as a therapeutic strategy. Here, an injectable thermosensitive hydroxypropyl chitin hydrogel incorporating Cu/Zn-doped bioactive glass particles, termed BG@HPCH, was developed for localized metalloimmunotherapy. BG incorporation improved the shear-thinning behavior, thermosensitive gelation, storage modulus, and stability of the hydrogel. In vitro, ionic release from BG@HPCH selectively reduced pathogenic B cell survival while preserving mesenchymal stem cell (MSC) viability. The optimized M-BG@HPCH increased the B cell dead-cell area from 1.93 ± 0.48% to 91.12 ± 0.90% at 24 h, while maintaining MSC viability at 98.59 ± 0.26% after 3 days. In TNF-transgenic mice, a single intra-articular injection of BG@HPCH reduced arthritis index scores from 2.88 ± 0.18 to 1.81 ± 0.13 at day 28, limited bone erosion, and showed no detectable systemic toxicity. Micro-CT analysis showed improved bone preservation, with BV/TV increasing from 30.00 ± 6.74% to 55.66 ± 1.07%. OCN staining further confirmed enhanced osteogenic activity, with the OCN+ area increasing by 2.16 times. Flow cytometry confirmed reduced B220+CD45.2+ B cell accumulation in treated joints. Single-cell RNA sequencing of 23,921 joint cells showed that BG@HPCH reduced inflammatory B cell, macrophage, and fibroblast subsets while expanding osteoblast-associated regenerative populations, accompanied by suppression of CD23- and CD74-associated B cell signaling axes. These findings establish BG@HPCH as a localized immunoregenerative biomaterial for coordinating pathogenic B cell depletion and bone repair in RA.

title: Communication breakdown: Impaired pericyte KATP channels in a model of Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Jackson WF
abstract: The brain requires a continuous supply of blood in proportion to its metabolic activity, a process that is disrupted in Alzheimer's disease. However, the mechanisms responsible for altered brain blood flow regulation in Alzheimer's disease remain poorly defined. In an earlier issue of JGP, Hariharan et al. (https://doi.org/10.1085/jgp.202614014) significantly add to our understanding of this pathology by showing that ATP-Sensitive K+ (KATP) channels in thin strand pericytes on cerebral capillaries are compromised at 6-8 weeks in the 5X-FAD mouse model of Alzheimer's disease. They also confirmed that cerebral capillary endothelial inward rectifier K+ (KIR) channels are crippled and importantly show that this defect occurs at 2-4 months, before significant cognitive defects have been reported. Combined, these channelopathies severely attenuate electrical communication along cerebral capillaries, dampening blood flow regulation. These novel findings present new therapeutic targets to slow or possibly prevent the reduced cerebral blood flow in Alzheimer's disease, perhaps delaying or preventing cognitive decline. Like all scientific advances, they also open the door for new areas of research.

title: Genetic Variation Underlying CSF Natural Killer T-Cell Frequency in Inflammatory CNS Diseases: A Genome-Wide Association Study.
authors: Wirsching L, Pukaj A, Held F, Makarov C, Kalluri SR, Grummel V, Peters L, Knier B
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Natural killer T (NKT) cells bridge innate and adaptive immunity and are implicated in immune regulation in autoimmune diseases. In multiple sclerosis (MS), reduced CSF frequencies of NKT cells have been reported, but their role in disease pathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we investigated the genetic architecture underlying CSF NKT cell frequency variability in individuals with MS and other CNS diseases. METHODS: We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) of CSF NKT cell frequencies in 456 individuals with MS, with replication in an independent cohort of 90 individuals with MS or other inflammatory CNS diseases. Functional follow-up assessed effects of the lead variant on integrin subunit beta 5 (ITGB5) gene expression in CSF CD4+ T cells, and Mendelian randomization (MR) analysis was used to evaluate causality. In addition, we examined associations of the lead variant and CSF NKT cell frequencies with MS disease severity as measured by the Age-Related Multiple Sclerosis Severity Score (ARMSS). RESULTS: We identified and replicated a novel genome-wide significant association of rs6783734*C (joint p = 4.57 x 10-9), an intronic variant in ITGB5 on chromosome 3, with increased CSF NKT cell frequencies. This association was absent in a control cohort of 368 individuals with other neurologic diseases (p = 1.4 × 10-1), suggesting a context-specific effect. rs6783734 was associated with reduced ITGB5 gene expression in CSF CD4+ T cells, and MR supported a causal relationship between ITGB5 expression and CSF NKT cell frequencies. Although rs6783734 was not associated with disease severity, higher CSF NKT cell frequencies were associated with greater ARMSS at the ≥1-year follow-up (p = 9.33 × 10-3). DISCUSSION: Our findings implicate ITGB5 as a potentially context-dependent modulator of immune cell dynamics in inflammatory CNS disease, linking genetic variation to NKT cell frequencies within the CNS compartment. Given the central role of integrins in immune cell trafficking and the therapeutic success of integrin-targeting agents in MS, these results highlight integrin-mediated pathways as determinants of CNS immune responses. Although the observed association of higher CSF NKT cell frequencies with greater disease severity suggests that integrating genetic factors and immune phenotypes may ultimately prove useful for patient stratification, this finding requires confirmation in larger studies.

title: Janus-structured piezoelectric membrane couples barrier protection with pathological microenvironment-responsive bioactivity for periodontal bone regeneration.
authors: Chen C, Sun J, Fang K, Miao W, Du X, Li J, Wen X, Qu Z
abstract: Periodontal bone regeneration remains challenging due to the persistent infection-inflammation-bone resorption cycle and the rapid invasion of epithelial and gingival connective tissues into defect sites. Here, we developed a biodegradable Janus membrane (J-PLLA-ZnO) based on poly(L-lactic acid) (PLLA) that spatially integrates barrier protection and pH-responsive bioactivity within a single construct. A dense PLLA layer facing soft tissues prevents premature tissue infiltration and maintains regenerative space, while a porous defect-facing interface functionalized with ZnO nanowires provides bioactive regulation. The ZnO nanowires enhance the overall piezoelectric response of the membrane and enable pH-responsive Zn2+ release under the acidic periodontal microenvironment, thereby delivering antibacterial, immunomodulatory, and osteogenic cues. In a rat periodontitis model, J-PLLA-ZnO rapidly suppressed infection-associated inflammation. One week after implantation, peripheral neutrophil percentage decreased to approximately 21% of those in the J-PLLA group, accompanied by reduced tumor necrosis factor-α expression and increased cluster of differentiation 206 expression, consistent with a shift toward a reparative macrophage phenotype. At week 6, J-PLLA-ZnO increased the osteocalcin-positive bone-forming area by approximately 1.5-fold compared with non-Janus PLLA-ZnO, indicating improved periodontal bone regeneration. Moreover, the cementoenamel junction-alveolar bone crest distance was reduced by approximately 40% relative to untreated controls. Meanwhile, the membrane underwent gradual biodegradation throughout the healing process. These findings demonstrate that integrating spatial barrier function with pH-responsive bioactivity represents a promising strategy for guided tissue regeneration in inflammatory periodontal defects.

title: Differential effects of amyloid-β and tau on UCH gene expression in Drosophila models of Alzheimer's disease.
authors: Arayesh MJ, Ataellahi F, Masoudi R
abstract: BACKGROUND: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a common neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive impairments in learning and memory. Substantial evidence indicates that dysfunction of the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS) in the AD brain leads to aberrant protein aggregation, ultimately resulting in synaptic dysfunction and neuronal loss. In this study, we investigated the effects of pan-neuronal expression of TauWT or Aβ42-key pathological hallmarks of AD-on the expression of UCH, a critical UPS component, in Drosophila melanogaster at three time points: 5, 15, and 25 days after eclosion. METHODS AND RESULTS: UCH mRNA levels were quantified using real-time RT-PCR. UCH expression showed an age-dependent downregulation in Aβ42 transgenic flies over all three post-eclosion intervals. While UCH transcription witnessed no significant change in 5-day-old TauWT transgenic flies, there was a considerable decline in UCH mRNA levels in 15- and 25-day-old flies. Notably, Aβ42 had a more prominent impact on UCH gene expression than TauWT across all three time points. CONCLUSION: TauWT and Aβ42 exert independent adverse effects on UCH expression. An apparent age-related trend was observed in the fly models, whereby Aβ42 showed a relatively stronger influence on UCH transcription compared with TauWT. Accordingly, therapeutic strategies that target both Tau and amyloid-β may warrant consideration.

title: Epstein-Barr Virus Serologic Profiles in Multiple Sclerosis and Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease.
authors: Kang YR, Kim KH, Heo N, Min JH, Kim W, Kim SW, Shin HY, Huh SY
abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVES: Although the link between Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) and multiple sclerosis (MS) is well established, geographic variation in EBV epidemiology warrants region-specific data from Asian populations. Beyond MS, the role of EBV in myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein antibody-associated disease (MOGAD) remains far less studied. This study aimed to compare EBV serostatus and antibody titers in patients with MS, MOGAD, and controls in a Korean cohort. METHODS: We analyzed MS (n = 130), MOGAD (n = 125), and untreated tumor controls without known EBV association (n = 132). MS and controls were frequency-matched to MOGAD by age at sampling. Serum Epstein-Barr nuclear antigen 1 (EBNA1) IgG, viral capsid antigen (VCA) IgG, VCA IgM, and early antigen (EA) IgG were measured using chemiluminescence immunoassays (LIAISON, DiaSorin). EBV seropositivity was defined as EBNA1 IgG or VCA IgG positivity, and serologic findings suggestive of possible recent infection/reactivation were defined as positivity for VCA IgM or EA IgG. RESULTS: EBV seropositivity was nearly universal in MS, MOGAD, and controls (98.5%, 98.4%, and 99.2%, p = 0.751). EBNA1 responses differed across groups, with the frequency of EBNA1 IgG levels exceeding the upper reportable limit (>600 U/mL) being highest in MS, compared with MOGAD and controls (66.2% vs 33.6% vs 43.9%; p < 0.001). In three-group analyses using controls as reference, MS had higher EBNA1 IgG levels (adjusted geometric mean ratio [aGMR], 1.54; p = 0.006), whereas MOGAD did not. For VCA IgG, MS did not differ from controls, whereas MOGAD showed lower levels than controls (aGMR, 0.72; p = 0.018). Among patients with MS and MOGAD, models additionally adjusted for disease-related factors indicated that EBNA1 IgG and VCA IgG levels were higher in MS (aGMR, 1.97; p < 0.001 and aGMR, 1.42; p = 0.018, respectively), while ongoing treatment at sampling was associated with lower VCA IgG levels (aGMR, 0.64; p = 0.007). Serologic findings suggestive of possible recent EBV infection or reactivation were comparable across groups. DISCUSSION: In this Korean cohort, MS showed stronger EBNA1 responses than MOGAD and controls, extending prior evidence on the relevance of EBNA1 in MS to an Asian population. The absence of a similar pattern in MOGAD suggests that the contribution of EBV may differ between the 2 diseases.

title: Prevalence and Clinical Significance of Gastric-Type Mucosal Lesions in Non-Ampullary Duodenal Epithelial Tumors Based on Mucin Phenotype.
authors: Ohno K, Nakatani E, Kurokami T, Kawai A, Matsuda M, Masui Y, Satoh T, Hirata T
abstract: OBJECTIVES: Non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors differ in clinicopathological features according to mucin phenotype. Gastric-type tumors have distinct biological features; however, their associated mucosal background remains unclear. In this study, gastric foveolar metaplasia, gastric heterotopia, and Brunner's gland hyperplasia were collectively referred to as gastric-type mucosal lesions (G-MLs). We aimed to assess their prevalence and associations with mucin phenotype and clinicopathological factors. METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the data of 130 patients with 130 resected non-ampullary duodenal epithelial tumors at a single center. Tumors were classified according to mucin phenotype. The prevalence of concomitant G-MLs and associated factors was evaluated. Exploratory Firth-penalized logistic regression analysis was used to assess the association between gastric-type tumors and G-ML presence. RESULTS: Concomitant G-MLs were identified in 44 patients (33.8%). Their prevalence was higher in gastric-type tumors (13/16; 81.3%) than in gastric-intestinal-type tumors (10/37; 27.0%) and intestinal-type tumors (21/77; 27.3%). G-MLs were associated with mild endoscopic gastric mucosal atrophy and smoking status and were inversely associated with current Helicobacter pylori infection. In the exploratory fully adjusted model, gastric-type tumors remained positively associated with the presence of G-MLs (adjusted odds ratio, 7.00; 95% confidence interval, 1.98-30.95; p = 0.002). CONCLUSIONS: G-MLs were present in approximately one-third of patients and were most frequent in gastric-type tumors. These findings indicate an association between G-MLs and gastric-type tumors; however, the cross-sectional design does not allow inference of a biological relationship. TRIAL REGISTRATION: N/A.

title: Inflammation-anchored injectable hydrogel integrating pathological nitric oxide scavenging and on-demand drug release for localized inflammatory bowel disease therapy.
authors: Eom S, Lee S, Boo Y, Kim J, Kim WJ
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing chronic relapsing gastrointestinal disorders, remains a profound clinical challenge because conventional therapeutics are often impeded by systemic off-target toxicities and suboptimal retention at inflamed mucosal sites. Herein, an inflammation-activated and retentive injectable hydrogel is presented, which leverages pathological nitric oxide (NO) overproduction as both a therapeutic target and an autonomous release trigger. An NO-responsive and NO-scavenging polymer (NRSP) incorporating an NO-cleavable o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) motif is formulated into cationic, dexamethasone-encapsulating micelles and electrostatically assembled with anionic hyaluronic acid (HA) to form a shear-thinning hydrogel that facilitates minimally invasive rectal administration and ensures prolonged, localized retention at the inflamed mucosal interface. Upon exposure to the NO-rich inflammatory microenvironment, structural disruption of NO-responsive and NO-scavenging micelles (NRSM) compromises the electrostatic integrity of the HA-micelle network, thereby reducing the storage modulus and accelerating cargo release. In vitro evaluations using lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages demonstrate that NRSM hydrogels effectively reduce intracellular and extracellular NO levels and attenuate pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Furthermore, the HA matrix mediates disease-adaptive localization through CD44 receptor recognition and preferential electrostatic adhesion to positively charged inflammatory interfaces, resulting in enhanced colonic retention in DSS-induced colitis models ex vivo. Following rectal administration in DSS-induced mice, NRSM-based hydrogels significantly alleviate disease severity, reduce colonic NO and inflammatory cytokine levels, and rescue mucosal architecture and mucin-associated features. Notably, dexamethasone-loaded NRSM hydrogel exerted the most potent synergistic therapeutic benefit. Overall, this disease-responsive hydrogel platform establishes an effective localized intervention for IBD, merging intrinsic pathological NO scavenging with controlled drug delivery.

title: Characterizing hypertension in activated PI3K delta syndrome: Findings from Epic Cosmos.
authors: Santiago B, Keelin J, Sun X, Chang C
abstract: APDS is a rare inborn error of immunity with comorbidity patterns that have yet to be characterized at a large scale. Using Epic Cosmos, a de-identified electronic health record database, we conducted a retrospective, cross-sectional analysis of 866 patients identified by structured diagnosis codes (ICD-10: D84.81; SNOMED: 793412000). Findings revealed that hypertension was coded as affecting 28.5% of the cohort, with age-stratified analyses demonstrating higher prevalence among younger APDS patients compared with age-matched non-APDS peers. Among patients aged ≤50 years, hypertension prevalence was 24.05% in the APDS group compared with 10.89% in the age-matched non-APDS population (prevalence ratio 2.21, 95% CI, 1.90-2.57, P < 0.0001). This association remained prominent in a more specific APDS sensitivity cohort in which the base population required an APDS diagnosis, alongside an allergy and immunology encounter. The findings of this paper provide large-scale characterization of APDS and identify hypertension, particularly among younger APDS patients, as a potentially underrecognized comorbidity that warrants further investigation.

title: Mosaic KRAS variants in childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus.
authors: Irabu H, Nishimura M, Sakura F, Asano T, Hatano M, Miyaoka F, Kaneko S, Shimbo A
abstract: Clinical targeted sequencing identified low-VAF KRAS variants in two of 26 children with childhood-onset systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE). Both had severe inflammatory manifestations but lacked Noonan syndrome features, and neither developed persistent lymphoproliferation suggestive of RAS-associated autoimmune lymphoproliferative disease during follow-up. These findings suggest that KRAS mosaicism may contribute to the development or severity of childhood-onset SLE.

title: The ups and downs of human UNC93B1: Autoimmune and viral conditions.
authors: Idiiatullina E, Casanova JL, Zhang SY
abstract: Mouse Unc93b1 was identified in 2006 by forward genetics as an ER membrane protein essential for the activity of the endosomal nucleic acid-sensing receptors TLR3, TLR7, and TLR9. In vitro studies in mouse and human cells have revealed its cellular functions, including ER-based stabilization and trafficking of endosomal TLR proteins (TLR3, TLR7, TLR8, and TLR9) and regulation of signaling thresholds through competitive trafficking control (TLR7 and TLR9). Human genetic studies have clarified the physiological role of UNC93B1 in natural conditions. Biallelic loss-of-function UNC93B1 mutations impair TLR3 signaling in central nervous system-resident cells, thereby conferring a predisposition to HSV-1 encephalitis. UNC93B1 deficiency may also predispose to other viral infections, as suggested by patients with inherited TLR3 or TLR7 deficiency. Conversely, monoallelic or biallelic UNC93B1 gain-of-function variants enhancing TLR7 and/or TLR8 signaling predispose patients to autoimmunity and inflammation, including early-onset systemic lupus erythematosus and chilblain lupus. Thus, in humans, UNC93B1 maintains a delicate balance between host defense and tolerance to self.

title: Genotype-phenotype analysis in 333 individuals with heterozygous variants in NFKB1.
authors: Armbruster SM, Caballero-Oteyza A, Bartsch O, Lorenzini T, Abolhassani H, Chan S, González Granado LI, Garcia-Bustos V
abstract: Heterozygous germline variants in NFKB1 can be classified into variants with "known protein defect" and "unknown protein effect." However, beyond this, NFKB1 variants may be additionally categorized into at least eight distinct variant classes. We conducted a literature review of 67 papers reporting on NFKB1 variants and included four additional individuals, carrying previously unreported NFKB1 variants. We identified 333 individuals with unique variants in NFKB1. Our compiled data revealed that there is no sex predilection, the penetrance-including all heterozygous carriers-was 78%, and the mean age of onset for the "known protein defect cohort" was 21.2 years. Individuals harboring variants with a known protein defect demonstrated a higher frequency of malignancies and autoimmune disorders. However, these individuals were less frequently classified as affected than individuals with variants with unknown protein defect. Carriers of whole NFKB1 gene deletions had a significantly higher penetrance to being designated as "affected," but beyond this, the clinical manifestations did not differ between variant classes.

title: Children's health before, during, and after parental/caregiver immigration detention in the United States: findings from a cross-sectional survey.
authors: Thapa K, Patler C, Saadi A
abstract: BACKGROUND: Parental immigration detention is a significant yet understudied stressor with potential consequences for children's well-being. We examined children's general health before, during, and after parental detention, and compared to the United States (US) pediatric population. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional household telephone survey in 2022-2023 of family members of immigrants detained by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement in 2020/21 and released on bond. Of 88 respondents, we analyzed data from 49 families with at least one school-aged minor child. Family members retrospectively reported on child health before, during, and after detention using the 7-item parent-report version of the PROMIS® Parent Proxy Scale- Global Health 7 measure, which provides standardized T-scores (mean = 50, SD = 10) benchmarked to the U.S. general population. FINDINGS: The mean T-scores were statistically equivalent to the population mean of 50 at pre-detention (49; 95% CI: 46.0, 52.0) and after release (48.9; 95% CI: 45.5, 52.4) but 17 T-score points (∼2 SD below the population mean) lower during detention (31.8; 95% CI: 28.6, 35.0), substantially exceeding the commonly accepted 5 T-score points threshold (half-SD) for clinically meaningful change. Reported problems for children during parental detention included decline in grades (n = 34, 69%), increased financial responsibilities (n = 29, 59%), household or caregiving responsibilities (n = 26, 53%), and food insecurity (n = 26, 53%). About 16% (n = 8) of children were unable to receive needed treatment or counseling from a mental health professional during parental detention. INTERPRETATION: Parental detention was associated with poorer reported child health, and reported health scores improved after release. Findings highlight the need for policies that consider the health consequences of immigration enforcement on children and families. FUNDING: This research was supported by the National Science Foundation and the Russell Sage Foundation and the Carnegie Corporation of New York.

title: Interactive effect of childhood adversity and HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation on alexithymia in adolescents.
authors: Zhou H, Lü W
abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood adversity increases risk for affective symptoms, including alexithymia, a transdiagnostic emotion-processing difficulty common in adolescence. Hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis-related genetic variation may contribute to individual differences in sensitivity to adverse environments. This study examined whether an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) moderated the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. METHODS: The present study addressed this issue in a sample of 460 adolescents (Mage = 12.73, SD = 0.72; 54.1% female) who completed the Childhood Trauma Questionnaire and the Toronto Alexithymia Scale. Saliva samples were collected for deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) genotyping, and an HPA-axis-related multilocus genetic profile score (MGPS) was constructed from six candidate polymorphisms. Hierarchical regression and re-parameterized regression analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Childhood adversity was positively associated with alexithymia. HPA-axis MGPS moderated this association. Specifically, adolescents with high HPA-axis MGPS exhibited higher levels of alexithymia when exposed to high childhood adversity but lower levels when exposed to low childhood adversity, providing preliminary support for the differential susceptibility model. LIMITATIONS: The cross-sectional design precludes causal inference, and the findings require replication in longitudinal, clinically enriched, and more diverse samples. CONCLUSIONS: HPA-axis multilocus genetic variation may function as a biological sensitivity factor in the association between childhood adversity and adolescent alexithymia. These findings extend gene-environment interaction research to alexithymia and highlight individual differences in adolescents' emotional responses to adversity.

title: Environmental sensitivity and perceived social support in relation to adolescent eating disorder symptoms.
authors: Mastromatteo LY, Tosi C, Cardi V, Cerolini S, Meregalli V, Baglioni C, Scrimin S
abstract: Eating disorders (EDs) frequently emerge during adolescence and are influenced by both individual and contextual factors. Among these, perceived social support has generally been associated with better outcomes, although findings remain inconsistent and may depend on both the source of support and individual differences in responsiveness to environmental inputs. The present study examined the role of Environmental Sensitivity (ES) and perceived social support in adolescent ED symptoms, focusing on different sources of support and their potential interaction within a vantage sensitivity framework. A sample of 466 adolescents (51.61% female; M = 14.80) completed self-report measures of ED symptoms, ES, and perceived social support. At a bivariate level, higher perceived support from family, teachers, friends, and peers was associated with lower ED symptoms. In covariate-adjusted models, only teachers' and family's support remained a significant predictor, while peer-related sources were no longer associated with ED symptoms. ES was consistently and positively associated with ED symptoms. Contrary to hypotheses, ES did not moderate the association between overall perceived social support and ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses suggested a sex-specific pattern, whereby the association between perceived social support and ED symptoms appeared to vary as a function of ES among males, but not females. These findings suggest that the association between social support and adolescent ED symptoms may depend on its source. Moreover, ES was consistently associated with ED symptoms. Exploratory analyses revealed that evidence for differential responsiveness to supportive contexts may vary by ES among males.

title: Input and uptake for complex syntactic structures in child language development: Implementing structural priming with diverse learner populations.
authors: Hao J, Sturt P, Rothman J, Chondrogianni V
abstract: Language development depends on both the quantity of linguistic input children receive and their ability to uptake input, yet the relationship between these two factors remains unclear. This study adopted the structural priming paradigm to examine how input and uptake shape syntactic development in three groups of Mandarin-speaking children aged 5-9 years (N = 75, Nfemale = 39): neurotypical monolinguals (optimal input and uptake), monolinguals with Developmental Language Disorder (optimal input, reduced uptake), and Mandarin-English heritage bilinguals (reduced input, optimal uptake). All groups had acquired the target non-canonical structures (the BA-, BEI-, and OSV-constructions). However, reduced input and reduced uptake were associated with distinct production patterns. Heritage bilinguals produced more canonical structures (the SVO-construction), whereas monolingual children, particularly those with Developmental Language Disorder, favoured the BA-construction, suggesting differences in underlying learning mechanisms and production strategies that may be shaped by their language (learning) experience. Moreover, while richer input enhanced uptake, reduced input did not diminish it, suggesting input quantity and processing ability play separable yet interacting roles in development.

Influence of perineal tears and body image disturbance on postpartum sexual quality of life: a cross-sectional study.
authors: Fillion D, Ruffolo AF, Verlet N, Martin C, Garabedian C, Rubod C, Kerbage Y, Cosson M
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: BACKGROUND: Whether perineal injury severity independently determines postpartum sexual quality of life (SQoL) is unclear. This study evaluated perineal tears and body image as determinants of SQoL and sexual resumption timing. METHODS: A total of 173 women (2-24 months postpartum, vaginal delivery) completed an online questionnaire including the SQoL-F and Body Image Scale (BIS). Women with perineal tear/episiotomy (PT/E; n = 118) were compared with those with an intact perineum (n = 51) using multivariate regression. RESULTS: SQoL-F scores were similar between groups (71.1 ± 23.3 vs 76.9 ± 24.0; p = 0.10), though PT/E delayed sexual resumption (p = 0.04). On multivariate analysis, SQoL-F was independently associated with dyspareunia (β = -10.96; p < 0.001), body image disturbance (β = -0.93; p < 0.001), and pre-pregnancy sexual satisfaction (β = +4.99; p = 0.001), but not tear type. Delayed resumption was independently associated with OASI (OR = 7.02; p = 0.02), first/second-degree tears (OR = 2.20; p = 0.04), and lower pre-pregnancy relationship satisfaction (OR = 0.50; p = 0.048). CONCLUSIONS: Postpartum SQoL is primarily determined by dyspareunia and body image disturbance rather than perineal tear severity. OASI carries a substantial risk of delayed sexual resumption, warranting dedicated postpartum counseling.

title: "Sailing Two Boats" the fragmented identity of working women and the hidden labor of infertility: a qualitative analysis.
authors: Dhar S, Poojari VG, Adiga P, Mundkur A, Tomar A, Kumar P
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: OBJECTIVE: To explore how professional women undergoing assisted reproductive technology (ART) experience and manage conflicts between treatment demands and professional identity; and to identify ways healthcare professionals can support them. METHODS: Following COREQ guidelines, semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 18 professional women undergoing ART in a tertiary care hospital. Reflexive Thematic Analysis bolstered by interdisciplinary investigator triangulation (clinical and basic science) ensured thematic confirmability. RESULTS: Analysis revealed Gendered Occupational Asymmetry (female occupational burden regardless of clinical aetiology), the Insider Paradox (the role reversal for healthcare professionals) and the Workplace Panopticon (constant self-surveillance to preserve professional authority). Interestingly, work simultaneously often acted as a Sanctuary of Competence, providing psychological respite. Finally, narratives exposed an Existential Rumination (mourning past personal-professional decisions) and permanent temporal career stalling. These themes were further mapped onto a 'A Day in the Life' structural framework to illustrate compounding daily burdens. CONCLUSIONS: Current clinical lifestyle directives inadequately account for the rigid psycho-socioeconomic structures governing professional women. Based on identified themes, we propose targeted measures for healthcare professionals to deliver patient-centric care by integrating occupational awareness and identity-sensitive counselling into routine ART practice, thereby potentially reducing distress and improving treatment experience.

title: Placental small-RNA sequencing reveals a distinct microRNA signature and its functional relevance in a preeclampsia rat model.
authors: Vaka R, Amaral LM, Chambers CL, Campbell N, Zheng B, Roman RJ, LaMarca B
abstract: OBJECTIVE: Despite extensive investigations over the last few decades, molecular mechanisms underlying the pathogenesis of preeclampsia remain incompletely understood. Emerging evidence suggests that microRNAs (miRNAs) regulate key pathological processes in preeclampsia including endothelial dysfunction, inflammation, and oxidative stress. However, a comprehensive profiling of miRNA expression has not been previously carried out. Thus, using reduced uterine perfusion pressure (RUPP) model of preeclampsia, we performed placental miRNA sequencing to identify functional relevance of abnormally expressed miRNAs. METHODS: Blood pressure was measured via carotid catheterization on gestational day (GD)19. Placental small-RNA sequencing was performed using Illumina NextSeq2000 sequencer. RESULTS: Our analysis identified 142 differentially regulated miRNAs (40 up- and 102 down-regulated) in placenta from RUPP rats. The top upregulated miRNAs included miR-211-3p, miR-628, miR-6324, miR-363-5p, and miR-6329, while miR-3587, miR-29b-3p, miR-3556a, miR-29a-3p, and miR-21-3p were the most downregulated. Functional annotation revealed associations with immune response (miR-363, miR-21, miR-29), B-cell differentiation (miR-628), T-cell activation (miR-21), adipogenesis, and lipid metabolism (miR-211, miR-29, miR-21), and angiogenesis (miR-363, miR-21). Further, gene ontology analysis revealed significant enrichment in biological processes; regulation of transport, cell-cell signaling, and calcium-dependent exocytosis, cellular components; synaptic vesicles, perinuclear cytoplasm, and clathrin-coated vesicles, and molecular functions; glycoprotein binding, protein dimerization, and myosin binding. CONCLUSION: These findings suggest that robust miRNA dysregulation in RUPP rats may underlie disease pathogenesis.

title: Coronavirus health beliefs and fetal health concerns: associations with preventive health behaviors during COVID-19.
authors: Nahum Yakovi S, Kushnir T
journal: Journal of psychosomatic obstetrics and gynaecology
abstract: OBJECTIVE: During infectious disease outbreaks, pregnant women and their fetuses may be especially vulnerable to health risks, emphasizing the importance of preventive health behaviors (PHB). The role of concerns about fetal health in shaping PHB during COVID-19 has never been examined. The present study examined the joint effect of concerns about fetal health and Coronavirus-related health beliefs (within the Health Belief Model) on PHB during COVID-19. METHODS: During the COVID-19 pandemic (September-November 2021), 202 pregnant Israeli women completed online questionnaires that assessed concerns about fetal health, health beliefs (perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, and barriers), and adherence to preventive health behaviors. Multiple hierarchical regression and mediation analyses were conducted. RESULTS: Concerns about fetal health were positively associated with PHB. Perceived susceptibility and perceived benefits were also positively associated with PHB, whereas perceived barriers were negatively associated; perceived severity was not significant. Mediation analyses indicated that concerns about fetal health fully mediated the association between perceived susceptibility and PHB and partially mediated the associations between perceived severity and perceived benefits and PHB. CONCLUSIONS: Concerns about fetal health play important direct and indirect roles in adhering to PHB during pregnancy. These findings may guide health services in developing tailored programs during pandemics.

title: Inter-arm blood pressure differences and blood pressure variability in early pregnancy: limited associations with pre-eclampsia.
authors: Skov HL, Riishede I, Rode L, Kirkegaard I, Pedersen LH, Sperling L, Nørgaard P, Jørgensen FS
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate an association of inter-arm blood pressure differences (IAD) and within-visit variability of blood pressure in early pregnancy with pre-eclampsia. METHODS: Blood pressure information was available on 8117 participants from the prospective PREeclampsia Screening In DEnmark (PRESIDE) study. Three consecutive blood pressure (BP) measurements were taken on both arms simultaneously in participants attending the first-trimester ultrasound. Maternal characteristics, medical history, and pregnancy outcome were collected. Outcomes were pre-eclampsia overall, further stratified into preterm (delivery < 37 weeks of gestation) and term cases (delivery ≥ 37 weeks of gestation). RESULTS: Women developing pre-eclampsia had a higher diastolic IAD (2.67 mmHg vs 2.33 mmHg) and pulse pressure IAD (4.67 mmHg vs 4.33 mmHg OR 1.04 (95% CI: 1.01; 1.07)). Pulse pressure IAD was associated with pre-eclampsia (adjusted OR 1.04, 95% CI 1.01, 1.07) and term pre-eclampsia (OR 1.05, 95 % CI 1.02, 1.08), but not with preterm pre-eclampsia (OR 0.99, 95% CI 0.9, 1.06). There were no associations between systolic IAD, within-visit BP variability and pre-eclampsia. CONCLUSION: Diastolic IAD and pulse pressure IAD in early pregnancy were higher in women developing pre-eclampsia. No association was found between systolic IAD or within-visit BP variability and pre-eclampsia.
